answer: Let chance pick the judges. If every answer is graded by a small panel drawn at random from a large pool, an attacker who spins up fifty identities cannot steer those seats toward his own work; most of his clones land grading strangers. Think of a jetty where boats dock in whatever slot the harbour beacon flashes, not the one the captain likes. To own a panel he would need a big share of the whole pool, not a single knoll of fake accounts, and that makes the attack cost grow with the network instead of staying flat.
